{{Short description|Mathematical function}}
{{Multiple issues|
{{context|date=May 2025}}
{{technical|date=May 2025}}
}}In applied mathematics, the '''reflecting function''' <math>\,F(t,x)</math> of a [[differential system]]  <math>\dot x=X(t,x)</math> connects the past state <math>\,x(-t)</math> of the system with the future state <math>\,x(t)</math> of the system by the formula <math>\,x(-t)=F(t,x(t)).</math> The concept of the reflecting function was introduced by [[Vladimir Mironenko|Uladzimir Ivanavich Mironenka]].

==Definition==
For the [[differential system]] <math>\dot x=X(t,x)</math> with the [[general solution]] <math>\varphi(t;t_0,x)</math> in [[Cauchy]] form, the Reflecting Function of the system is defined by the formula <math>F(t,x)=\varphi(-t;t,x).</math>

==Application==
If a vector-function <math>X(t,x)</math> is <math>\,2\omega</math>-periodic with respect to <math>\,t</math>, then <math>\,F(-\omega,x)</math> is the in-period <math>\,[-\omega;\omega]</math> transformation ([[Poincaré map]]) of the differential system <math>\dot x=X(t,x).</math> Therefore the knowledge of the Reflecting Function give us the opportunity to find out the initial dates <math>\,(\omega,x_0)</math> of [[periodic solution]]s of the differential system <math>\dot x=X(t,x)</math> and investigate the [[Lyapunov stability|stability]] of those solutions.

For the Reflecting Function <math>\,F(t,x)</math> of the system <math>\dot x=X(t,x)</math> the basic relation 

: <math>\,F_t+F_x X+X(-t,F)=0,\qquad F(0,x)=x.</math>

is holding.

Therefore we have an opportunity sometimes to find Poincaré map of the non-integrable in [[Numerical integration|quadrature]] systems even in [[elementary functions]].
